tws-edifier-tws1-pro-2.review: Warm, wide sound; actually OK, but the codec is still SBC, and the treble still sounds compressed. The soundstage is actually pleasant; it's only the treble that's a pity. Mic and ANC are very OK too.

tws-samsung-galaxy-buds-core.review: Just a repackaged Buds FE: newer, with a newer warranty and battery. Ordinary, more or less the same as the Buds FE. Muddy in the bass, warm vocals, but a bit bright again at 10 kHz. ANC and fit are good; maybe one of the quietest under a million rupiah. The mic is very ordinary, even compared with Moondrop or EarFun. If you want a bean shape with good sound under 1 million, it's still the Free Pro 3. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-samsung-buds-fe.review: Lots of people ask. A bit muddy, bassy, no custom EQ, a very ordinary mic. Its strengths: the Samsung name, plus OK ANC and fit. Why is the ANC OK? Because the fit is: it seals the ear really well and has an extra rubber fin to close the seal. Good passive isolation, good ANC. The rest, not really. Only for people who need ANC and don't care about EQ; you don't need me to convince you. If you like it, just buy it. Totally fine. Done.

tws-vyatta-airboom-pro-s.review: Has custom EQ via the Tuya app, and the EQ is saved straight onto the TWS. Fit is OK, 32-hour battery. Shame many people say it breaks easily.

tws-vyatta-airboom-smart.review: Skip to the SoundPeats Clear or R50i NC.

tws-huawei-freebuds-se.review: You can buy a single replacement bud if you lose one, or buy the case separately. V-shaped sound, punchy, powerful bass. Most people will like this. Better than the R100 and P2i. Nothing special; the Dot 3i is better.

tws-baseus-bowie-m2s.review: The driver is weird and bad. With an EQ preset the driver sounds good, but a FLAT custom EQ changes it completely. However much I fiddled, it couldn't be saved to sound even as nice as the Dot 3i. The Dot 3i's driver is superior; this one's resolution isn't clear. It's not a tuning problem, it's the driver. The rest is fine though: ANC and mic not bad.

tws-eggel-quietbuds-neo.review: Sound is decent and EQable, but the EQ isn't practical: you have to save before you hear the effect. Limited controls: changing volume means no play/pause, only double and triple tap. ANC is there, that's about it. Not recommended. At this budget, skip ANC; better a big battery like the SoundPeats Clear.

tws-edifier-x3s.review: The sound is bright. Such a pity. The mic's not bad. It has aptX, but if it's bright it's hard to enjoy.

tws-fantech-mithril-tx1-pro.review: Safe, pleasant tuning: the bass is there and the vocals are clear. Fun but safe. Has a gaming mode, though only AAC. Worth it at this price, with EQ and a find-my-TWS feature.

tws-vyatta-airboom-anc.review: If you want to try a TWS with ANC, this is a good start: even at only −25 dB you can feel the ANC. Annoyingly, the sound isn't great, but it's safe, not painful. Boomy and warm. The case and buds feel a bit flimsy too. The cool part: a 12-month replace-with-new warranty (terms apply).

tws-soundcore-p2i.review: Skip to the R50i or SoundPeats Clear.

tws-soundcore-r50i.review: Warm, wide in the bass and low-mids. A murky driver, though not as murky as the T3. Not stunning. Wide in the bass. Of the 22 EQ presets, only Piano, Bass Reducer and Treble Booster are usable. Good mic, but the Nakamichi TW018S's mic is better. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-soundpeats-t3-pro.review: Muffled. You can't feel the ANC. A muffled driver is like a bad LED monitor panel or a poor camera sensor: whatever you show on it, raising sharpness or contrast won't make it good. Same with a murky driver: no custom EQ can save it. Just save up for the Clear. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-realme-t110.review: Skip to the SoundPeats Clear or R50i NC.

tws-nakamichi-tw018s.review: Nice, smooth sounding. Fairly balanced with more emphasis on sub-bass. Not muddled. Smoother than the R50i; the R50i is punchier with a wider soundstage. Good mic.

tws-soundtech-s16.review: Skip to the R50i NC or Clear.

tws-soundcore-a20i.review: Muffled and warm, with slightly more bass than the R50i. For consumers overall I'd say get the R50i: better mic, and a fun sound too. This one's mids are even murkier, and the R50i's battery is bigger.

tws-soundpeats-truefree-2.review: Ugh, how does something like this go viral? I really can't believe you all told me to buy this. A murky, muffled driver. The R50i is already muffled, yet it's clearer than this with its BASS REDUCER EQ, and the R50i's battery is bigger (30 hours) with a gaming mode too. Big case, big buds with an awkward fit, and a small battery. Weird. A waste of money, told to buy this T_T

tws-eggel-energy-buds-pro.review: Too boomy, which is not good for me. The bass is truly off the rails. Weak mic too.

tws-dbe-seikabuds-pro-elite.review: Muffled, basically. The Clear and Tozo have better drivers. Skip. Overpriced.

tws-dbe-tws10.review: The first TWS from dBe, an Indonesian audio brand. Not bad for music, but the PistonBuds have more features.

tws-1more-pistonbuds.review: Cheap but still OK; only the highs are a bit unclear. Wide soundstage in the bass. Over 300 units sold through his TikTok account.

tws-moondrop-robin.review: Not worth reviewing. Bad. Incoherent. The highs are too tizzy. At 1.9 million rupiah you'd be buying something far too overpriced. Maybe only for weeb collectors, or as a fashion accessory.

tws-aukey.review: This one has too much bass.

tws-baseus-encok-wm02.review: Just skip it, don't buy it. Not good.

tws-baseus-e19.review: Murky resolution, no app support, bad mic, a very bassy, boomy, bloated tuning. Skip to the Realme T110 or Soundcore R50i.

tws-jabra-elite-2.review: Overpriced. The tuning is safe, but there's no properly adjustable ANC like the 1More ComfoBuds Pro. EQ is still preset-only, plus find-my-TWS. Not bad, but plenty are better, like the Dot 3i.

tws-jbl-live-flex-3.review: The best-sounding half in-ear TWS. The timbre is insane, very natural. Bite, bright and clear; the mids open up the soundstage a lot. The bass slams too, with a wide rumble. The ANC is noticeable, not as quiet as AirPods, but it doesn't make you queasy either. This is probably the best JBL TWS out there; no half in-ear sounds like this yet. Ironically JBL's sealed in-ear models still trail other TWS on average.

tws-airpods-4-anc.review: Good driver, wide and spacious. The default tuning is a bit piercing and sibilant up top. Good width in the imaging, and the ANC is the quietest of the unsealed ones I've tried (sealed TWS are still quieter), though over time it gives a headache and ear pressure. Downside: no app for Android or Mac users, only iPad/iPhone. No custom EQ. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-oppo-enco-air5s.review: An alternative to the non-Pro AirPods. Mic OK, EQ OK, sound OK. ANC is ordinary. The app works on iOS, Android and even MacBook. In the same class as the Xiaomi Buds 5, though the shell isn't as slippery; nearly identical to the Xiaomi with small tuning differences. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-xiaomi-buds-5.review: A god-tier driver for an unsealed TWS. The bass spreads wide and the rumble is lovely. Fuller resolution than the K20i, Block etc. It doesn't need to go deep in the ear to sound right. Harman tuning and custom EQ. The adaptive ANC that adjusts to your ear shape makes a difference, but it'll never be as quiet as a TWS with eartips. Good mic. Custom buttons are great. Just the budget, oh my. (Review on his YouTube.)

tws-sennheiser-accentum-open.review: The default tonality is fairly balanced and good, slightly boosted up top; mid to sub-bass is very balanced. Good fit. The material is a bit matte, not glossy like Xiaomi/Samsung/JBL, so it's less prone to shifting in the ear and the sound stays stable. No app for EQ yet, no ANC. Standard mic. 2-year warranty.

tws-samsung-buds-3.review: Mid-bass to sub-bass is fairly boosted, which comes across as muffled; cut around 500, 250, 100 and 60 Hz to get more clarity in the mids and highs. The fit locks in more and isn't as slippery as the Xiaomi Buds 5, so the ANC can perform better, though still not like a sealed TWS. Why pick this as a Samsung user? If you dislike rubber eartips and want multipoint and lower latency. Otherwise very usable on any Android.

tws-tozo-a3.review: More bass than the K20i and easier for me to tune. Very OK. Bassy with OK rumble. The fit doesn't shift easily either. Imaging and soundstage are still very ordinary. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-soundcore-k20i.review: For those who don't like rubber eartips, this is bassy enough with clear mids and treble. Custom EQ, a low-latency gaming mode, customisable controls. Lovely, and only around 100k rupiah. It really beats the SoundPeats Air 4 Lite on value; Soundcore slashed the price. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-soundpeats-air-5.review: Shouty upper mids, plasticky and mushy timbre there. There are presets to match the sound to your ear shape; number 2 suits me better, and I could custom-EQ further, but the app's EQ isn't enough to adjust the frequencies that need it. And the price is in a very awkward spot: you can get a Xiaomi with better value, in my view. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-moondrop-block.review: Good imaging, clear separation, like there's wide space to the left and right. The tonality is very neutral. The bass is present, but the fit doesn't grip much. Flathead style; maybe long-time earbud fans who want a TWS will accept this. Quite neutral, with a lot of lower mids in my view. If you just want a cheap TWS with lots of features and a good mic, the K20i is more than enough.

tws-soundpeats-air4-lite.review: The fit is really nice: half in-ear, but the part facing the ear canal sits nicely. EQable. Lovely. Not as detailed as a sealed TWS, but lots of features: LDAC, EQ, multipoint.

tws-rapatech-air-dual-enc-ii.review: The bass really comes through. Push it too far into the ear and it gets too bassy, but shift it a little and it sits just right, pleasant and balanced. The mic is very OK too. Fair price, good mic and sound quality. The only downside is no app, but for a half in-ear the sound is very OK. 2-YEAR WARRANTY.

tws-soundcore-life-note3s.review: I don't like TWS without rubber eartips, but this is one of the nicely featured half in-ear/earbud types. It has CUSTOM EQ, bro. The cream colour is cool. Fit is OK. REALLY GOOD MIC.

tws-huawei-freebuds-se-2.review: An unsealed TWS with a good mic and a good battery. Has EQ presets. You can feel the bass. No left/right lag.

tws-sabbat-x12-pro.review: Shaped like AirPods-style earbuds, so no eartips and it doesn't sink deep into the ear. A pleasant tuning, balanced and fun; the vocals aren't peaky or sharp. Nice. Just not many features. Also, its controls are pressed like a button on the ear, not touch.
